Title: How to Fix Missing Virtual Game Cards on Nintendo Switch After Update
IntroLines: Are your virtual game cards missing from your Nintendo Switch after a recent update?
In this video, I'll walk you through 3 quick fixes to restore and unhide your missing game cards.

Sections.Heading: SOLUTION 1: UNHIDE CARDS FROM THE HIDDEN SOFTWARE MENU
Steps: •  First, from your HOME Menu, open " Virtual Game Cards " from the bottom toolbar.
•  Choose your primary user profile linked to your Nintendo Account.
•  Scroll all the way down to the bottom of your software list.
•  Select " Hidden Software " .
•  Enter your account password or parental PIN if prompted.
•  Highlight the missing virtual game card you want to restore.
•  Press the " + " button on your Joy-Con or controller to open options.
•  Select " Unhide " to return it to your active library.
•  Finally, return to your main virtual cards list and verify that the game has reappeared.
Sections.Bridge: If your virtual game cards are still not appearing, let's refresh your online license settings.

Sections.Heading: SOLUTION 2: REFRESH ONLINE LICENSES IN USER SETTINGS
Steps: •  First, from your HOME Menu, open " System Settings " .
•  Scroll down the left sidebar and select " Users " .
•  Select your user profile.
•  Scroll down on the right side and select " Online License Settings " .
•  Ensure that the toggle for " Use Online Licenses " is turned " On " .
•  Select " Check License Status " to force a sync with Nintendo's servers.
•  Wait a few seconds for your account permissions to refresh.
•  Finally, return to your HOME Menu and check if your virtual game cards have reloaded.
Sections.Bridge: If your cards are still missing from your screen, let's restore them directly from the eShop.

Sections.Heading: SOLUTION 3: REDOWNLOAD LICENSES FROM THE NINTENDO ESHOP
Steps: •  First, open the " Nintendo eShop " from the bottom toolbar of your HOME Menu.
•  Select the user profile that originally purchased the games.
•  Navigate to your " User Icon " in the top-right corner.
•  Scroll down the left sidebar and select " Redownload " .
•  Browse through your purchased software list to find your missing game.
•  Select the " Cloud Download " icon next to the title.
•  Wait for your Switch to re-index the software and license card.
•  Finally, return to your HOME Menu and launch the game to confirm it is fully working.

OutroLines: And that's how you can fix missing virtual game cards on your Nintendo Switch after an update.
